verdict.delta_sentence: Compared with gc-decomp-harness, this board offers equally strong tinted grouping and semantic flow color but has a more repetitive section rhythm and several longer cross-board return routes.

sub_checks.name: frame_use
sub_checks.note: The three broad rows fill the locked frame evenly with comfortable outer margins and no major dead band, though the lower-right area is somewhat lighter than the rest.

sub_checks.name: corridors_and_air
sub_checks.note: Most section gaps and label chips have ample breathing room, but the dense rollback, audit, and healthy-progression connections in the middle-lower row reduce corridor clarity.

sub_checks.name: grouping
sub_checks.note: Fifteen numbered, softly tinted regions clearly decompose the process, with each region generally holding only two or three related nodes.

sub_checks.name: color
sub_checks.note: Blue, purple, orange, green, teal, and red consistently distinguish flow families, with red dashed failure paths and green healthy progression carrying clear semantics.

sub_checks.name: machinery_leakage
sub_checks.note: No crosshair junctions, exposed waypoints, or orphaned badges are visible; the only slight craft distraction is the oversized arrow-shaped traffic and progression nodes.

sub_checks.name: alignment_and_rhythm
sub_checks.note: Strong column registers and repeated section dimensions create a stable rhythm, although the uniform card treatment is more repetitive and less compositionally varied than gc-decomp-harness.

sub_checks.name: edge_legibility
sub_checks.note: Edges are mostly clean and crossing-free, but several very long horizontal return runs and the tightly interleaved lower-center rollback, revision, and threshold paths require extra tracing.

verdict.rank_order_sanity_note: The assigned scores and visual ordering agree: gc-decomp-harness and the board under grade are approximately tied at 7.5, both ranking slightly above intent-classification-2 at 7.0.
